newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Bank Negara to cut 700 staff in stages - Deputy PM.
newsitem.headline: Bank Negara to cut 700 staff in stages - Deputy PM.

text.p: Malaysia's central bank Bank Negara will likely cut over 700 of its staff in stages as it automates its operations, Deputy Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim said on Monday.
The national news agency Bernama said Bank Negara employs about 2,000 people.

"With the availability of electronic mail and other sophisticated facilities, there is no necessity for many branches. Bank Negara should maintain its standards and should not employ more staff than it requires," he said.
The news agency report did not say over what period the programme would be implemented.
Bernama quoted Anwar, who is also Finance Minister, as telling reporters that the reduction in staff was being conducted under a "voluntary separation" programme.
Under the plan, the central bank would also close down several of its 12 branches, Anwar said.
He said the programme was being implemented at a time when it was easy for the affected to find alternative employment in Malaysia's rapidly expanding financial services sector.

He was quoted as saying that this programme followed Governor Ahmad Don's assessment that many positions in the central bank were not needed with the increasing technological sophistication in the banking industry.
